text: Not every row parses cleanly. A wrong delimiter, an extra column, a stray quote — something eventually breaks, and Snowflake has to decide what to do about it.

Here's what an error actually looks like in Snowsight. This particular one is a dropped-table error, not a load, but a bad COPY INTO surfaces exactly the same way: an error code, then the real message underneath.
ON_ERROR controls what happens next. The default, ABORT_STATEMENT, fails loud at the first bad row. Setting it to CONTINUE instead skips just that row and keeps going.
Before you commit to a load at all, VALIDATION_MODE set to RETURN_ERRORS runs a dry run — it reports every row that would fail, and loads nothing into the table.
And checking after the fact isn't limited to a SQL function. Copy History sits right under Query History in the UI, as its own tab specifically for load status.
That same information is queryable directly. COPY_HISTORY needs a table name and a time window by design, and filtering to error_count greater than zero shows you exactly which files had problems.
Next: the lab. Stage, file format, COPY INTO, and error handling — all four, on one real dataset, in one sitting.
